# Jobs

11 endpoints, all GET. Base URL `https://www.socialcrawl.dev`, auth header `x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY`.

**Credit costs:** 3 standard (1 credit), 4 advanced (5), 4 premium (10) - the exact cost is in each endpoint heading below.

Job listings across four boards in one shape: LinkedIn, Indeed, Bing, and Xing each get a keyword/location search plus single-listing detail, on the canonical Job / JobList schemas. Also LinkedIn organization-id resolution (feed the ids back into the LinkedIn search filters) and salary ranges by job title and country with title suggestions. Search endpoints are premium (10cr); detail is advanced (5cr); the salary and organization lookups are 1cr.

## GET /v1/jobs/bing - 5 credits (advanced)

Returns one Bing-aggregated job: title, company, location, employment type, description, and apply URL. Use an id from GET /v1/jobs/bing/search.

**Use when** Use it after bing/search, passing a job id from that list to read the description and apply link.
**Cost** cache 600 s
**Paging** none

**Query params**

- `id` (required) - Bing job id from bing/search. · e.g. `MTE5OTc2NjYxOS5SZXRybw==`

**Response** `Job` object at `data`, `{ job }` ([full schema](schemas/Job.md))

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `job.title` |  |
| `job.id` |  |
| `job.url` |  |
| `job.company.name` |  |
| `job.apply_url` |  |
| `job.description` |  |

+16 more (types in the full schema): `job` {employment_type, experience_level, listed_at, location, remote}; `job.ext` {accepting_applications, applicant_count, board, country_code, industries, job_function, job_provider, linkedin_company_name, salary_currency, salary_max, salary_min}. Also in the sample: `job.company` {id null, url null, verified null} (+1 more).

```bash
curl -G "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/jobs/bing" \
  --data-urlencode "id=MTE5OTc2NjYxOS5SZXRybw==" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

## GET /v1/jobs/bing/search - 10 credits (premium)

Returns aggregated job listings from Bing matching a keyword and location, with optional date, employment type, and remote-only filters. Each row has title, company, location, and the original job board. List rows do not include an apply URL; pass an id to GET /v1/jobs/bing for the description and apply link. location is required on page 1.

**Use when** you want to search across boards in one call, then pass an id to bing for the description and apply URL. location is required on page 1.
**Cost** cache 120 s
**Empty results** An upstream 404 means "zero items", not "not found" - you get `200 {items: []}` and a refund.
**Paging** cursor · ≈20/page (observed once) · depth unknown · N items ≈ ceil(N/20) x 10 credits

**Query params**

- `query` (optional, string) - Keywords, job title, or company name. · e.g. `software engineer`
- `location` (optional, string) - City or country. Required on page 1. · e.g. `United States`
- `date_posted` (optional, enum: week | day) - Maximum age: week or day. · e.g. `week`
- `employment_types` (optional, string) - Semicolon-separated: contractor, fulltime, parttime, temporary.
- `remote_only` (optional, boolean) - When true, only remote listings.
- `cursor` (optional, string) - Opaque cursor from the previous page.

**Constraints**

- Provide at least one of `query`, `cursor`.
- Provide at least one of `location`, `cursor`.

**Response** `JobList` rows at `data.items[]`, each `{ job }` ([full schema](schemas/JobList.md))

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `job.title` |  |
| `job.id` |  |
| `job.url` |  |
| `job.company.name` |  |
| `job.apply_url` |  |
| `job.description` |  |

+16 more (types in the full schema): `job` {employment_type, experience_level, listed_at, location, remote}; `job.ext` {accepting_applications, applicant_count, board, country_code, industries, job_function, job_provider, linkedin_company_name, salary_currency, salary_max, salary_min}. Also in the sample: `job.company` {id null, url null, verified null} (+1 more). Page-level: `data.dropped`.

```bash
curl -G "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/jobs/bing/search" \
  --data-urlencode "query=software engineer" \
  --data-urlencode "location=United States" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

## GET /v1/jobs/indeed/search - 10 credits (premium)

Returns Indeed job listings matching a keyword, country, and optional city, sort, and radius. Each row includes title, company, location, description, and apply URL. country_code is required on page 1 (ISO 3166-1 alpha-2). Page 2 with the cursor from page 1.

**Use when** you want to search Indeed in a given country, optionally narrowing by city, sort, and radius, then pass an id to indeed. country_code is required on page 1.
**Cost** cache 120 s
**Empty results** An upstream 404 means "zero items", not "not found" - you get `200 {items: []}` and a refund.
**Paging** cursor · ≈20/page (observed once) · depth unknown · N items ≈ ceil(N/20) x 10 credits

**Query params**

- `query` (optional, string) - Keywords, job title, or company name. · e.g. `software engineer`
- `location` (optional, string) - City or region within the country. · e.g. `San Francisco`
- `country_code` (optional, string) - ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code (for example us, de, kr). · e.g. `us`
- `sort_type` (optional, enum: relevance | date) - relevance (default) or date.
- `radius` (optional, integer, min 0) - Distance from location.
- `radius_type` (optional, enum: km | miles) - km (default) or miles.
- `cursor` (optional, string) - Opaque cursor from the previous page.

**Constraints**

- Provide at least one of `query`, `cursor`.
- Provide at least one of `country_code`, `cursor`.

**Response** `JobList` rows at `data.items[]`, each `{ job }` ([full schema](schemas/JobList.md))

+16 more (types in the full schema): `job` {employment_type, experience_level, listed_at, location, remote}; `job.ext` {accepting_applications, applicant_count, board, country_code, industries, job_function, job_provider, linkedin_company_name, salary_currency, salary_max, salary_min}. Also in the sample: `job.company` {id null, url null, verified null} (+1 more). Page-level: `data.dropped`.

## GET /v1/jobs/linkedin/organizations - 1 credit (standard)

Returns LinkedIn companies and schools matching a name, each with a display name and numeric id. Pass those ids as organization_ids on GET /v1/jobs/linkedin/search to filter listings by employer.

**Use when** Use it first to turn an employer name into the organization_ids filter that linkedin/search accepts.
**Cost** cache 120 s
**Paging** single page - Fixed-window lookup: upstream returns one non-cursored page of organization ids.

**Query params**

- `query` (required) - Company or school name. · e.g. `google`

**Response** `SearchResult` rows at `data.items[]`, each `{ displayName, id }` (inferred from a sample): {displayName string, id string}.

Page-level: `data.dropped`.

```bash
curl -G "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/jobs/linkedin/organizations" \
  --data-urlencode "query=google" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

## GET /v1/jobs/salary - 1 credit (standard)

Returns min, max, mean, and median pay for a job title in a country, broken out hourly, daily, weekly, monthly, and yearly, plus the local currency. Use GET /v1/jobs/salary/titles first when the title is uncertain.

**Use when** Use it after salary/titles when you have a known title and want the pay band for that country.
**Cost** cache 1800 s
**Paging** none

**Query params**

- `query` (required) - Job title, preferably one returned by salary/titles. · e.g. `software engineer`
- `country_code` (required) - ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code. · e.g. `us`

**Response** `Analytics` object at `data` (inferred from a sample): {country string, countryCode string, currency string, lastUpdatedTimestamp number}; `dailySalary` {max number, mean number, median number, min number}; `hourlySalary` {max number, mean number, median number, min number}; `monthlySalary` {max number, mean number, median number, min number}; `weeklySalary` {max number, mean number, median number, min number}; `yearlySalary` {max number, mean number, median number, min number}.

```bash
curl -G "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/jobs/salary" \
  --data-urlencode "query=software engineer" \
  --data-urlencode "country_code=us" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

## GET /v1/jobs/salary/titles - 1 credit (standard)

Returns known job titles matching a query in a country, each with a listing count. Use a returned title as query on GET /v1/jobs/salary.

**Use when** Use it first to turn a loose query into a title that salary will accept.
**Cost** cache 1800 s
**Paging** none

**Query params**

- `query` (required) - Partial job title (for example programming, nurse). · e.g. `software`
- `country_code` (required) - ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code. · e.g. `us`

**Response** `Analytics` object at `data`, `{ jobTitles }` (inferred from a sample): `jobTitles[]` {count number, jobTitle string}.

```bash
curl -G "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/jobs/salary/titles" \
  --data-urlencode "query=software" \
  --data-urlencode "country_code=us" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

## GET /v1/jobs/xing/search - 10 credits (premium)

Returns Xing job listings matching a keyword, with optional German-language location, date, employment type, career level, remote option, and minimum yearly salary filters. Rows often include a salary range. Page 2 with the cursor from page 1.

**Use when** you want to search the German-language job market with location, date, career level, remote, and minimum-salary filters, then pass an id to xing.
**Cost** cache 120 s
**Empty results** An upstream 404 means "zero items", not "not found" - you get `200 {items: []}` and a refund.
**Paging** cursor · ≈10/page (observed once) · depth unknown · N items ≈ ceil(N/10) x 10 credits

**Query params**

- `location` (optional, string) - City or country, preferably in German (for example Berlin, Schweiz). · e.g. `Berlin`
